Subject: Pilot success charter & model pairing — GlobeTrek trial

Hi Lisa / Andrew —

Great conversation earlier today. Summarizing next steps and a proposed success charter so we have a single source of truth heading into the pilot kickoff. Please review and call out anything missing.

Objective: validate a lightweight NLU + triage pipeline to automatically classify support emails into intent buckets and surface high-priority routing recommendations for agents (reduce manual triage).

Proposed pilot scope (2 weeks):
- Dataset: 5k anonymized recent support emails (English + ES/FR/PT priority locales)
- Models to evaluate: primary candidate = Llama-3-13B (q4_0) from our open-model catalog; fallback candidate = Mistral-7B-instruct (q3) for lower-latency scenarios
- Success criteria (pass/fail hooks):
  - Intent classification accuracy (F1) >= 0.85 on labelled holdout
  - 95th percentile response latency (inference) <= 300ms for single-request path
  - Label coverage: support intents properly covered for ES/FR/PT (target >= 80% of frequent intents per locale)
  - Human review acceptance: >= 90% of top-50 routing suggestions judged useful by agents in a short A/B panel

Evaluation plan:
- Week 0 (prep): dataset extract + schema mapping, sandbox S3 access, prompt/template checklist
- Week 1: run inference on 3k samples vs both models (parallel), collect metrics (latency, tokens, accuracy), human review panel of 50 samples per locale
- Week 2: refine prompts/biasing, run final 2k samples, produce a final report with recommended model + quantization/ops profile

Operational notes / constraints:
- We will instrument prefix caching and a KV cache where feasible; Marcus will recommend batching/kv settings during kickoff.
- We propose starting with 13B quantized profile to balance accuracy/latency; fallback 7B for cheaper bursts.

Ownership (proposed):
- AE / primary contact: Vanessa Ortiz (Redwood)
- Solutions lead (technical): Marcus Lin (Redwood)
- Customer success / trial ops: Priyom Das (Redwood)
- Customer data owner: Lisa Park (GlobeTrek)

Deliverables attached: GlobeTrek_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (template), sample_prompts.csv (example prompt sets).

Next steps:
1) Confirm dataset export window + who will provide the anonymized S3 link (Lisa)
2) Kickoff meeting: propose Tue 2026-12-22 10:00 PT (30m)
3) Marcus to share model runbook + quant profiles for review (internal)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Quick technical note for the thread:

- Model pairing rationale: Llama-3-13B (q4) gives the best balance against our target F1 for multi-intent classification while still staying in a sub-350ms median on A100-like infra with prefix caching. Mistral-7B-instruct is a good fallback for burst/low-cost runs when we can accept slightly lower accuracy.
- Quant/profile: recommend q4_0 for primary, q3 for fallback. We'll test KV-cache enabled for sequences with repeated context (agent history).
- Multilingual coverage: for LatAm Spanish we need to seed prompts with 100 locale-specific examples to avoid regression; I will prepare a short prompt-localization doc.
- Data access: preferred flow is an s3:// path with read-only IAM role for our sandbox account; Lisa, if you prefer other transport (Secure FTP), let us know.

Attachment: model_rundown.md (high-level notes + param/cost estimate).

I'll prepare a short sample run to estimate token counts and expected cost for a 5k sample job — should have that before the kickoff.

— Marcus
